steps: 1. Open global search. 2. Type: ZZAUTOTEST 3. Look at the left-hand side of every result row. 4. Check that a customer row, an asset row, a vendor row, a part row and a work order row each carry an icon, and that rows of the SAME kind carry the SAME icon.
expected: Every result row shows a small icon on its left, and the icon differs by record type so you can tell at a glance what each row is. In V1 each type had its own icon: a building for a customer, a contact card for a contact match, a truck for an asset, a shopfront for a vendor, and a tools icon for work orders, part sales and parts. title: The keyboard shortcut is shown in the search box so people can find it
steps: 1. Look at the search box in the header WITHOUT clicking it. 2. Check whether the keyboard shortcut is written in or beside the box. 3. Hover over it and read any tooltip. 4. On a Mac the hint should read the Command symbol and K; on Windows it should read Ctrl+K. 5. Narrow the window to tablet width and look again.
expected: The keyboard shortcut is visible on the search box on a desktop-width screen, and it shows the RIGHT one for the machine you are on - the Command symbol with K on a Mac, Ctrl+K on Windows. Hovering explains what it does. In V1 this hint was deliberately shown so people would discover the shortcut instead of reaching for the mouse every time.
